diagnostic_evidence.quote: The summation limits $z_{\min} = \max_i(a_i)$ and $z_{\max} = \min_y(b_y)$ are governed by the linear combinations
$\mathcal{R}_z \gets$ compute cyclotomic factorization of the ratio via Eq.~\eqref{eq:ratio_Rz}
$\{\mathcal{R}_z\}$ is the sequence of multiplicative update ratios computed via Eq.~\eqref{eq:ratio_Rz}

issues.failure_explanation: From the paper's own summand, $T_{z+1}/T_z = -[z+2]_q\,\prod_y[b_y-z]_q / \prod_i[z+1-a_i]_q$: since $[z+1-a_i]! = [z+1-a_i]\cdot[z-a_i]!$, the factors $[z+1-a_i]_q$ belong in the ratio's denominator, and since $[b_y-z-1]! = [b_y-z]!/[b_y-z]$, the factors $[b_y-z]_q$ belong in its numerator. Eq. (ratio_Rz) swaps the two products and uses $[b_y-(z+1)]_q$ instead of $[b_y-z]_q$. Concrete checks: for $\{1\,1\,1;1\,1\,1\}$ ($a_i=3$, $b_y=4$), $T_4/T_3 = -[5]_q$, while Eq. (ratio_Rz) gives $-[5]_q[1]_q^4/[0]_q^3$, a division by $[0]_q=0$; for $\{2\,2\,2;2\,2\,2\}$, $T_7/T_6 = -[8]_q[2]_q^3$, not $-[8]_q$. Moreover, because $z_{\max}=\min_y b_y$, the denominator of Eq. (ratio_Rz) always contains $[b_y-(z_{\max})]_q=[0]_q=0$ at $z=z_{\max}-1$, so the final update ratio is always singular. Hence the DCR built 'via Eq. (ratio_Rz)' (DCR definition, Algorithm 1, Algorithm 2) does not encode the series it claims to represent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side of Eq. (ratio_Rz) by the correct ratio $-[z+2]_q\prod_y[b_y-z]_q/\prod_i[z+1-a_i]_q$, a routine derivation from Eq. (racah_6j); all downstream constructions and algorithms then work unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The recurrence of Sec. 3.3, the DCR definition, Algorithm alg:compilation and Algorithm alg:projection as written produce wrong summand values and a guaranteed division by zero at the last update step, so the compiled object does not represent the series; Prop. deformation_as_evaluation consequently fails for 6j-type series.
issues.title: Hypergeometric update ratio Eq. (ratio_Rz) is incorrect (products swapped, b-index off by one) and always singular at the last step
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, forced algebraic correction (rederivable directly from Eq. racah_6j in the source) that preserves every substantive claim, guarantee, rate and scope; no new lemma, construction or replacement argument is needed. It is not a pure typo because the construction depends on the erroneous formula and the correction must be rederived, but its repair burden and mathematical loss are nil.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The intrinsic sensitivity of the problem is governed by the condition number (Eq.~\eqref{eq:condition_num}), which is independent of representation.
While both engines ultimately utilize LSE to safely accumulate the final alternating sum, the DCR engine pre-conditions the calculation.
The residual error at large $j$ is governed by the intrinsic condition number $\kappa$, confirming that the DCR has exhausted the representation-level improvement.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition number $\kappa = \sum_z|T_z|/|S|$ (Eq. condition_num) measures cancellation between the final summands and the sum. The DCR still evaluates the alternating sum $\sum_z(-1)^zT_z$ of the reduced summands numerically (Algorithm alg:projection; the paper itself states both engines use LSE to accumulate the final alternating sum), and the paper's own analysis keeps the intrinsic $\mathcal{O}(\kappa Z\epsilon)$ error term, states that $\kappa$ is representation-independent, and reports that the DCR's residual error at large $j$ is governed by $\kappa$ (the DCR already has ~433% relative error at $j=110$, $k=500$, in Table tab:phase_flip). Only the intra-summand numerator/denominator cancellations ($\gamma_{\text{rep}}$) are resolved at the exponent level; the $\kappa$-cancellation between summands is not resolved algebraically.

failure_location.quote: In particular, the large intermediate cancellations to resolve the condition number $\kappa$ in Section~\ref{subsec:cancellation} are no longer realized numerically, but are instead resolved exactly at the algebraic level.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the claim to the mechanism established elsewhere in the paper: exact resolution of intra-summand cancellations (dynamic-range/$\gamma_{\text{rep}}$ compression), with the intrinsic $\kappa$-limited summation error remaining.
issues.overall_effect: The mechanistic justification of the 'algebraic preconditioner' claim misstates what the framework achieves; a reader is led to believe the DCR escapes the intrinsic condition number, contradicting the paper's own error analysis (Sec. 6.2) and empirical results (Sec. 7.2).
issues.title: False claim that condition-number (kappa) cancellations are 'resolved exactly at the algebraic level'
issues.why_classification: A local rewording, consistent with the paper's own Eq. (forwd_error), complexity analysis and benchmark data, preserves all results and guarantees; no mathematical content is lost since the correct mechanism is already established in the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Both components have integer exponents and are evaluated exactly by integer arithmetic.
The entire square root is resolved at the exponent level, without field extension and without any polynomial computation.

issues.failure_explanation: The evaluation map is defined (Eq. project_monomial) only on cyclotomic monomials, but $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{DCR}}$ is a tuple containing the square-free part $\mathcal{M}_{\rm rad}$, whose evaluation requires $\sqrt{\Pi_q(\mathcal{M}_{\rm rad})}$ (the return statement of Algorithm alg:projection) — an operation outside the stated definition with two possible values. No branch/sign convention is given, although the sign of the amplitude (e.g. of the 6j prefactor $\prod\Delta_{abc}$, a square root of a factorial ratio) depends on it, so the claimed equality is not well defined and the proof ('Since $\Pi_q$ is multiplicative, the result follows') does not establish it. The supporting claims are also false as written: the square root is not 'evaluated exactly by integer arithmetic', and it is not resolved 'without field extension': by the paper's own formulas the classical 6j $\{1\,1\,2;1\,2\,1\}$ equals $-1/(2\sqrt{5})$, so exact evaluation requires $\sqrt{5}\notin\mathbb{Q}$, and membership of the needed square root in the exact target $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{2h})$ is never established. 'Any admissible value of $q$' is moreover undefined (admissibility is defined for spins, not for $q$).

failure_location.quote: Then for any admissible value of $q$, $S(q) = \Pi_q(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{DCR}})$, where $\Pi_q$ denotes the evaluation map defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:project_monomial}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the square-root semantics of the projection: fix a branch/sign convention (e.g. the standard sign convention for the $\Delta_{abc}$ prefactors, or continuity from real $q\in(0,1)$), add the corresponding sign handling to Algorithm alg:projection, prove the convention reproduces $S(q)$, and qualify the exact-evaluation claims (the square root may require a quadratic extension or a symbolic square-root representation, as the classical limit already shows).
issues.overall_effect: The central exactness claim — evaluation equals a projection of a fixed combinatorial object — is ill-defined as stated; the exact projection regime ($\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{2h})$) and the classical-limit regime inherit unproven field-membership assumptions, and the sign of projected amplitudes is undetermined by the specification.
issues.title: Projection of the DCR is undefined on its square-root part: branch/sign unspecified and 'no field extension'/'integer arithmetic' claims false
issues.why_classification: A supported resolution avoiding new global architecture exists (branch/sign convention plus qualification of the 'integer arithmetic'/'no field extension' claims), but it requires a contained nontrivial argument (correctness of the sign convention) and a limited weakening of the advertised exact-evaluation capabilities.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $z_{\min}, z_{\max} \gets$ determine summation bounds from admissibility conditions
while a negative exponent produces a pole
In particular, all topological levels $k$ and the classical limit $q \to 1$ arise from the same data $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{DCR}}$ via different projection maps.
We demonstrate that admissibility at roots of unity, $q$-deformation, and classical limits manifest as intrinsic properties of a single DCR combinatorial object.

issues.failure_explanation: Prop. admissibility establishes only a monomial-level criterion (vanishing iff the $\Phi_h$-exponent is positive). The prose claims admissibility itself is internalized: violating terms are 'annihilated under projection' and admissibility becomes 'a vanishing condition internal to the representation, rather than an externally imposed constraint'. For the actual level-$k$ admissibility of the 6j (triad sums $\le k = h-2$), violations are not annihilated: by the paper's own formulas ($[m]_q=0$ iff $h\mid m$, Prop. cyclo_fact; Eq. tri_coeff), a triad with $a+b+c\ge h-1$ makes $[a+b+c+1]_q!$ vanish, so $\Delta_{abc}$ has a pole, while the summand numerators $[z+1]_q!$ also vanish — the projection is $0/0$-indeterminate (e.g. spins $(3,3,0,3,3,3)$ at $h=5$ give a net pole), not zero. Admissibility is in fact imposed externally (Algorithm alg:compilation determines the summation bounds from admissibility conditions), and the claim that 'all topological levels $k$' arise from the same DCR fails for levels below the spin content, where the projection is singular.

failure_location.quote: Terms violating admissibility are annihilated under projection, and in practical implementations this can lead to early termination of summations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the claims: cyclotomic vanishing captures the summation cutoff for admissible spins (where the projection is pole-free), while spin/level admissibility must still be imposed externally, and admissibility-violating projections are singular (poles or indeterminate) rather than annihilated; weaken contribution (5) and the abstract accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The structural claim that admissibility at roots of unity is an intrinsic property of the DCR (abstract, contribution (5), Secs. 5.1–5.2) is unreliable, and the advertised scope ('all topological levels $k$' from one compiled object) overstates what the projection supports; the early-termination story covers only the admissible, pole-free case.
issues.title: Admissibility at roots of unity is not internalized as cyclotomic vanishing: violating terms are singular (poles/0-0), not 'annihilated'
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening with local rewording and no new proof architecture, but a substantive advertised claim (admissibility as an intrinsic vanishing property of the DCR, one of the five listed contributions) must be withdrawn or heavily qualified, so it is more than minor.
